subproblem.title: C¹ push-forward of an integer multiplicity triple carried by a compact set is a current supported in the image
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n), K ⊆ U compact with Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), O ⊆ ℝ^P open with K ⊆ O, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on O with f(K) ⊆ U. Then there is Q ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) with Q(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), where Df(x) = fderiv ℝ f x and (α∘L)(v₁, …, vₙ) = α(Lv₁, …, Lvₙ) (α.compContinuousLinearMap L); moreover spt Q is compact and spt Q ⊆ f(K). This is f_#τ(M, θ, ξ) of Simon Ch. 6, 2.23–2.24(2).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U K O : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ K) = 0 → IsOpen O → K ⊆ O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → f '' K ⊆ U → ∃ Q : GeometricCurrentOn U n, (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Q ω = ∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∂μHE[n]) ∧ IsCompact Q.support ∧ Q.support ⊆ f '' K
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5(a)–(b) of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 2.23–2.24(2), chapter-06.txt lines 403–440), specialized to a compact set K in place of F = B̄_t(y), the open set O in place of B_r(y), and a general f in place of π. The hypothesis Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 replaces the parent's step 2(a) ("μ_X is carried by F").
Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; μ := Hⁿ⌞M. ‖·‖ denotes operator norms (of linear maps, of n-covectors as continuous alternating maps, and of n-vectors as functionals on n-covectors). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) put β_ω(x) := ω(f(x))∘Df(x) (= (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) and ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_z ‖ω(z)‖, which is finite because ω is continuous with compact support.
1. Derivative bound. Since f is C¹ on the open set O, f and x ↦ Df(x) are continuous on O (Mathlib ContDiffOn.continuousOn, ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen). K ⊆ O is compact, so Λ_K := sup_{x∈K} ‖Df(x)‖ < ∞ (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn; take Λ_K := 0 if K = ∅).
2. Pointwise bound. For every n-covector α and linear L, ‖α∘L‖ ≤ ‖α‖·‖L‖ⁿ (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_compContinuousLinearMap_le). Hence ‖β_ω(x)‖ ≤ ‖ω‖_∞·Λ_Kⁿ for every x ∈ K.
3. Orientation bound. By the field R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there are an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) and s ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(x)(β) = s·β(τ) for every n-covector β. At such x, |ξ(x)(β)| = |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖·Π_i|τ_i| = ‖β‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm). (This is the content of the accepted DAG declaration dpf_pfc_imrep_orient_abs_apply_le; a decomposition of this node may reuse it.)
4. Measurability. On O the map x ↦ β_ω(x) is continuous (ω, f and Df are continuous there, and (α, L) ↦ α∘L is continuous), so x ↦ 1_K(x)·β_ω(x) is Borel. Since μ(ℝ^P ∖ K) = Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 (M is Borel), the integrand x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(β_ω(x)) agrees μ-a.e. with x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(1_K(x)β_ω(x)), which is μ-a.e. strongly measurable: θ is Borel, ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, and evaluation (ζ, β) ↦ ζ(β) is continuous.
5. Integrability and the basic estimate. By steps 2–4, |θ(x)ξ(x)(β_ω(x))| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞·Λ_Kⁿ·θ(x)·1_K(x) for μ-a.e. x, and c_K := ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult (K is compact and K ⊆ U). So the integrand is μ-integrable, and I(ω) := ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(β_ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) satisfies |I(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞·Λ_Kⁿ·c_K. (Accepted DAG declaration dpf_pfc_imrep_pairing_integrable_abs_le has exactly this form with C := K and F := 1_K·β_ω.)
6. Linearity. β_{aω+bη}(x) = a·β_ω(x) + b·β_η(x) for a, b ∈ ℝ, because evaluation at f(x) is linear and α ↦ α∘L is linear. As ξ(x) is linear and all integrands are integrable (step 5), I(aω + bη) = a·I(ω) + b·I(η). So I is a linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U).
7. Continuity. Let ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U), i.e. TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0: there is a compact C ⊆ U with tsupport ω_j ⊆ C for all j, and the k = 0 clause says ω_j → 0 uniformly on C (iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j is ω_j composed with the norm-preserving curry0 equivalence). Since ω_j = 0 off C, ‖ω_j‖_∞ → 0 (accepted DAG declaration dpf_pfc_testFormOnConverges_zero_uniform). By step 5, |I(ω_j)| ≤ ‖ω_j‖_∞·Λ_Kⁿ·c_K → 0. Hence Q := I is a GeometricCurrentOn U n, and Q(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
8. Vanishing away from f(K). Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ∩ f(K) = ∅. For x ∈ K, f(x) ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(f(x)) = 0 and β_ω(x) = 0. The integrand vanishes on M ∩ K, hence μ-a.e. (Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0), and Q(ω) = 0.
9. Support. f is continuous on K, so f(K) is compact, hence closed; and f(K) ⊆ U by hypothesis. Let z ∈ U ∖ f(K). Since U ∖ f(K) is open, there is s > 0 with closedBall(z, s) ⊆ U ∖ f(K). The ball W := ball(z, s) is open, closure W = closedBall(z, s) (s ≠ 0) is compact and contained in U, and Q vanishes on W: if tsupport ω ⊆ W then tsupport ω ∩ f(K) = ∅, so Q(ω) = 0 by step 8. Thus W belongs to the family whose union is the zero region of Q (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.zeroRegion), z ∈ zeroRegion(Q), and z ∉ spt Q = U ∖ zeroRegion(Q). As spt Q ⊆ U by definition, spt Q ⊆ f(K).
10. Compactness. From spt Q = U ∖ zeroRegion(Q), spt Q ⊆ f(K) and f(K) ⊆ U we get spt Q = f(K) ∖ zeroRegion(Q) = f(K) ∩ (zeroRegion Q)ᶜ. The zero region is open (a union of open sets), so spt Q is a closed subset of the compact set f(K), hence compact. ∎
proof_key_steps: Df is continuous on O, so ‖Df‖ ≤ Λ_K on the compact K; unit orientations satisfy |ξ(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ and ‖α∘L‖ ≤ ‖α‖‖L‖ⁿ.
Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 makes the integrand a.e. equal to a bounded Borel integrand supported in M ∩ K, so it is integrable with |Q(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞Λ_Kⁿ∫_{M∩K}θ.
Linearity is pointwise; test-form convergence forces ‖ω_j‖_∞ → 0, giving sequential continuity, so Q is a GeometricCurrentOn U n.
Forms vanishing on the compact f(K) give Q = 0, so every point of U ∖ f(K) has a ball in the zero region: spt Q ⊆ f(K).
spt Q = f(K) minus the open zero region is a closed subset of the compact f(K), hence compact.

audit.reason: The prose and Lean type match. Compact derivative bounds and locally integrable multiplicity justify the integral, linearity and sequential continuity. The zero-region argument establishes support containment and compactness without circular reliance.
